run.question:
Alertmanager alert KubePodNotReady (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xprwb since 2026-11-25T18:48:13Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is caused by a Deployment rollout of otel-demo/product-catalog to an image that cannot be pulled. The pod named in the alert, product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xprwb, is in phase Pending with its only application container unready and waiting in ImagePullBackOff: the kubelet reports 'failed to resolve reference "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1": ... not found'. That pod was created at 18:47:58Z by a new ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f, after the Deployment product-catalog (revision 2, generation 2) was updated to that image; managedFields shows helm Apply at 18:40:28Z and an Update by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 18:47:58Z. kubelet events record 5 Failed pulls and 20 Back-off events for the image, and the Deployment status shows replicas 2, readyReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1, with the Progressing condition citing ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f. The previous ReplicaSet product-catalog-658dcdbc87 (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog) still has its one replica Running and Ready, the product-catalog Service endpoints contain only that pod, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready stayed at 1 through the window, and product-catalog spans in the last 10 minutes carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so no service-level request errors or traffic loss from the bad replica were observed. The flagd fault-injection flags that concern product catalog (productCatalogFailure, productCatalogLockContention) are both at defaultVariant 'off', so a flagd-injected product-catalog fault was considered and rejected. Observed error-status spans for ad, payment, fraud-detection, recommendation and flagd at small rates are not tied to this rollout by any evidence and are treated as background.

claims.text: Pod otel-demo/product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xprwb (owner ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f, node kind-environment-worker, startTime 2026-11-25T18:47:58Z) is in phase Pending with Ready and ContainersReady conditions False (reason ContainersNotReady); its container product-catalog is not ready, restartCount 0, state waiting with reason ImagePullBackOff and message 'Back-off pulling image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1": ErrImagePull: rpc error: code = NotFound desc = failed to pull and unpack image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1": failed to resolve reference "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1": quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1: not found'.

Kubelet events for pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xprwb record 5 'Failed to pull image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1"' Warning events (18:48:01Z-18:50:50Z), 5 'Error: ErrImagePull' Warning events, 20 BackOff events ('Back-off pulling image ...') and 20 'Error: ImagePullBackOff' Warning events between 18:48:25Z and 18:53:04Z.

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog is at annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2, generation 2, with spec.template container product-catalog image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1, and status replicas=2, readyReplicas=1, updatedReplicas=1, unavailableReplicas=1, Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable) and Progressing=True with message 'ReplicaSet "product-catalog-7b499ffb4f" is progressing.' (lastUpdateTime 2026-11-25T18:47:58Z).

The Deployment's metadata.managedFieldsSummary lists only three managers: helm (Apply, 2026-11-25T18:40:28Z), OpenAPI-Generator (Update, 2026-11-25T18:47:58Z) and kube-controller-manager (status Update, 2026-11-25T18:47:58Z); the OpenAPI-Generator update coincides with the creation of ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f.

Deployment product-catalog owns two ReplicaSets: product-catalog-658dcdbc87 (created 18:40:31Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog, 1/1 ready) and product-catalog-7b499ffb4f (created 18:47:58Z, image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1, replicas 1 with no readyReplicas).

The product-catalog Service's endpoint subset contains only address 10.244.2.162 targeting Pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-5m689 (port tcp-service 8080); the new Pending pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xprwb is not an endpoint address.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace="otel-demo",deployment="product-catalog"} is 1 at every sampled point from 18:41:00Z through 18:53:00Z, so the rollout did not reduce the Deployment's ready replica count during the alert window.

For service product-catalog, the only traces_span_metrics_calls_total series with a non-UNSET status in the 10 minutes before 18:53:00Z is absent: the increase is returned solely under status_code=STATUS_CODE_UNSET (value 13890.53 spans), i.e. no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for product-catalog was returned for that window.

ConfigMap flagd-config data demo.flagd.json declares flag productCatalogFailure with defaultVariant "off" (description 'Fail product catalog service on a specific product') and flag productCatalogLockContention with defaultVariant "off"; all flags in the file show defaultVariant values that are off/zero, so no product-catalog fault flag was in an on state.

The firing alert rule KubePodNotReady (group kubernetes-apps, 30s interval) evaluates phase Pending|Unknown and Running-with-ready=0, with duration 300 seconds; its alert instance for pod otel-demo/product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xprwb has activeAt 2026-11-25T18:48:13.549939497Z and state firing, while the same rule also fires for pod itbench-observability/prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0 (activeAt 18:37:43Z, not investigated here).

Within namespace otel-demo only Deployment product-catalog carries an image matching 'it-bench' (quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1, ready 1, unavailable 1, revision 2); no other otel-demo Deployment's containers use that registry path.

All other 26 pods in namespace otel-demo are phase Running with Ready=True and restartCount 0 (including product-catalog-658dcdbc87-5m689), so the non-ready condition is confined to product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-xprwb; no other otel-demo pod shows a failed or unready container in the pod listing taken at 18:53:23Z.

No user-visible error was observed on the frontend in the 10 minutes before 18:53:00Z: the STATUS_CODE_ERROR series returned for service frontend has value 0 (and frontend-proxy / cart / accounting / load-generator also return 0), while product-catalog returns no ERROR series at all.

A flagd-injected product-catalog fault (productCatalogFailure / productCatalogLockContention) as the trigger was considered and rejected: both flags are declared with defaultVariant 'off' in ConfigMap flagd-config and the pod failure is a kubelet image-resolution error, not an application-level error.

The Deployment product-catalog was rolled to a nonexistent image by the external API client recorded as manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 18:47:58Z; because no change-history integration is available and managedFieldsSummary keeps only each manager's last write, what that actor is or why the tag was chosen remains a hypothesis rather than an observed fact.

Restore the Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog's container image to the previously working ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog (or to a tag that exists in quay.io/it-bench), then confirm the new ReplicaSet's pod becomes Ready and the Deployment's unavailableReplicas returns to 0; separately identify the 'OpenAPI-Generator' client that applied the 18:47:58Z image update so the bad tag is not reapplied.

gaps: The actor recorded as manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' and its intent cannot be verified: the change_history integration is not available, and managedFieldsSummary gives only the last write per manager, not which fields changed or any earlier writes.

The alert annotation text says the pod has been non-ready for longer than 15 minutes, but the pod's own status.startTime is 2026-11-25T18:47:58Z, the rule's duration is 300s, and the alert's activeAt is 18:48:13Z; the reason for this timing discrepancy is not explained by the evidence collected.

Application-log health of the still-serving pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-5m689 was not confirmed: the filtered log query for that pod returned no lines (status no_data, evidence_id eec95c0c-5d11-4f29-8bd0-139e831d9e50-t1:a6785e48-30f5-4e2c-9487-f87b0a9c0cd1) for 18:43:00Z-18:53:21Z, and the Pending pod has no container logs because its container never started.

The trace search by tag error=true for service product-catalog over 18:43:00Z-18:53:21Z returned no data (evidence_id cecffa6c-42f4-4149-9d94-31591a05ffdb-t0:8fe02f27-4fa7-4056-8fcb-bd17d55160fc), so span-level error attribution for product-catalog is unchecked rather than proven absent by that view.

No baseline before 18:43:00Z was established for the small STATUS_CODE_ERROR rates observed on ad, payment, fraud-detection, recommendation and flagd, so they cannot be classified as background versus incident-related; they are not tied to the product-catalog rollout by any evidence.

End-to-end user impact was not verified beyond span-status signals: frontend request-level success/failure and load-generator behavior were not inspected, so customer impact remains unverified rather than excluded.
A second KubePodNotReady alert is firing for pod itbench-observability/prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0 (activeAt 18:37:43Z); it is outside this alert's object and was not investigated.
next_steps: Revert or correct the product-catalog container image on Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog and watch the replacement ReplicaSet's pod reach Ready.
Audit which system authenticates as the 'OpenAPI-Generator' field manager and gate that client from setting non-existent image tags in otel-demo.
If readiness of the serving replica matters operationally, add a before-window baseline comparison of product-catalog and frontend error rates so future rollouts can be judged against it.

rules.query: sum by (namespace, pod, job, cluster) (max by (namespace, pod, job, cluster) (kube_pod_status_phase{job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*",phase=~"Pending|Unknown"} or (kube_pod_status_phase{job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*",phase="Running"} == 1 and on (namespace, pod, cluster) kube_pod_status_ready{condition="true",job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*"} == 0)) * on (namespace, pod, cluster) group_left () topk by (namespace, pod, cluster) (1, max by (namespace, pod, owner_kind, cluster) (kube_pod_owner{owner_kind!="Job"}))) > 0 unless on (namespace, pod, cluster) kube_pod_status_reason{job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*",reason="SchedulingGated"} == 1
